name: Data Engineering Consulting
title: Data Engineering & ETL Consulting Services | MV.tech
description: Hire remote data engineers for Python and SQL pipelines, BigQuery, Redshift and reliable reporting. Senior specialists with flexible timezone overlap.
intro: Get dependable data from the systems you already use. MV.tech builds and improves ingestion pipelines, cloud warehouses and reporting models so your team can work with consistent, current information.
fitHeading: When your data needs engineering attention
fit: Reports depend on spreadsheets, recurring exports or someone remembering to run a script.
A dashboard refresh succeeds, but the underlying numbers are incomplete or out of date.
API changes, duplicate records and failed jobs make every reporting cycle a repair exercise.
Your product team needs a data engineer alongside its existing developers.

deliverables.title: ETL and ELT pipelines
deliverables.text: Bring data from APIs, files and databases into a repeatable ingestion process. Define incremental loads, retries, backfills and duplicate handling around the behavior of each source.

deliverables.title: Cloud warehouses and SQL models
deliverables.text: Design BigQuery or Redshift tables, transformations and reporting models. Make business definitions, table ownership and refresh dependencies explicit before expanding the platform.

deliverables.title: Data quality and observability
deliverables.text: Check freshness, completeness and reconciliation at meaningful boundaries. Add useful logs and failure alerts so a successful job is not mistaken for trustworthy data.

deliverables.title: Reporting and handover
deliverables.text: Connect validated datasets to Tableau, dashboards or downstream applications. Include source mappings, operating notes and recovery steps in the agreed handover.

scopeHeading: A useful first project: one dependable reporting flow
scope: Start with a business report that matters and trace its path back to the source. Agree which records belong in the result, how fresh they need to be and how correctness will be checked. Then scope the ingestion, transformations and reporting output together. This gives the project a concrete acceptance test before more sources or dashboards are added.

approach.title: Map sources and definitions
approach.text: Review access, API limits, data volumes, history requirements and the business meaning of the metrics.

approach.title: Build and reconcile
approach.text: Implement the pipeline and compare the output with source records, including empty periods, updates and retries.

approach.title: Operate and extend
approach.text: Document schedules, ownership and recovery. Agree support and the next useful source or reporting model.

questions.question: Can you improve an existing pipeline without rebuilding everything?
questions.answer: Yes. We can start with a bounded review of your existing Python, SQL, cloud and reporting workflows. The scope can focus on unreliable jobs, missing validation, slow queries or a specific integration, preserving the parts that already work.

questions.question: Can you work alongside our internal engineering team?
questions.answer: Yes. MV.tech can own an agreed data workstream or provide specialist capacity alongside your team. We agree responsibilities, access, review steps and overlapping working hours before delivery begins.

questions.question: How is a data engineering project priced?
questions.answer: The estimate depends on source count, access complexity, historical data volume, transformation rules, freshness needs and support. Our remote operating model keeps overhead lean; a useful comparison includes monitoring, documentation and handover as well as the initial build.

questions.question: What should we share before the first call?
questions.answer: Share the report or workflow you want to improve, the source systems, approximate data volumes, current tools and required refresh frequency. A description or sanitized example is enough for an initial conversation; credentials are not needed in an enquiry.

name: AI Automation, RAG & MCP Development
title: AI Automation, RAG & MCP Development Services | MV.tech
description: Build AI automation, RAG systems, MCP servers and custom AI solutions with MV.tech's senior remote consultants. Connect business data, tools and workflows.
intro: Turn a specific business problem into a useful AI solution. MV.tech builds AI automation, retrieval-augmented generation systems, Model Context Protocol (MCP) integrations and custom assistants that connect approved company knowledge, tools and workflows.
fitHeading: Start with a workflow people already need
fit: Employees spend time searching through documents to answer recurring operational questions.
A prototype chatbot gives plausible answers but cannot show where they came from.
Your product needs an assistant that can use approved business data, APIs or tools through MCP.
You need engineering help to evaluate and integrate an AI feature into an existing application.

deliverables.title: RAG and knowledge search
deliverables.text: Plan document ingestion, retrieval and source references around a defined knowledge collection. Account for updates, permissions and questions the available material cannot answer.

deliverables.title: AI automation and custom assistants
deliverables.text: Connect an assistant to a support workflow, internal tool or customer application. Automate agreed steps, define permitted actions and keep a person in control of approvals and exceptions.

deliverables.title: MCP server and tool development
deliverables.text: Build Model Context Protocol servers that expose approved tools and data to compatible AI applications. Define tool inputs, resource access, authorization and logging around the business systems being connected.

deliverables.title: Custom AI solutions
deliverables.text: Integrate document processing, classification, extraction or decision support into an existing workflow. Agree the expected output, validation rules and review path before automating a business action.

deliverables.title: LLM and API integration
deliverables.text: Bring model responses into existing business logic and user interfaces. Validate inputs and outputs, handle failures and keep application permissions under server-side control.

deliverables.title: Evaluation and operating controls
deliverables.text: Agree representative questions and expected behavior. Review source grounding, unsupported answers, latency and usage cost before expanding the feature's audience.

scopeHeading: A useful first project: a bounded knowledge assistant
scope: Choose a defined set of documents and a small group of users. Collect questions they actually ask, including questions outside the documents' scope. A first release can then be assessed against source references, correct handling of missing information and the time it takes to find an answer. Wider access and automated actions can be scoped after those fundamentals are clear.

approach.title: Define the question and data
approach.text: Identify users, approved sources, permissions and the decisions the assistant will support.

approach.title: Build and evaluate
approach.text: Connect retrieval, model behavior and the interface. Test with real questions and review failure cases.

approach.title: Integrate and monitor
approach.text: Release within an agreed scope, track answer quality and usage, and document the update process.

questions.question: What is retrieval-augmented generation, or RAG?
questions.answer: RAG retrieves relevant material from an approved source collection and provides it to a language model when generating an answer. It can help an assistant answer questions about your own information, but retrieval quality, access controls and evaluation still matter.

questions.question: What is MCP development?
questions.answer: Model Context Protocol (MCP) provides a shared interface for AI applications to connect to tools and data. We can build an MCP server around your approved APIs or systems, define the tools and resources it exposes, and test it with the intended compatible clients. Access permissions and approval requirements remain part of the application design.

questions.question: Do we need to train our own AI model?
questions.answer: Not necessarily. The right scope may use an existing model with retrieval and application integration. We review your use case, data, evaluation criteria and operating constraints before proposing an approach.

questions.question: Can the assistant respect different user permissions?
questions.answer: Role-aware access can be part of the scope. The design must enforce authorization before protected data is retrieved or an action is performed; instructions written into a prompt are not a substitute for application access controls.

questions.question: What determines the cost of an AI assistant?
questions.answer: The main factors are source preparation, integrations, permission rules, evaluation, user interface and support. Ongoing costs also depend on model usage, retrieval infrastructure and traffic. These should be considered alongside the build estimate.

name: Workflow Automation Consulting
title: Workflow Automation & API Integration Services | MV.tech
description: Automate repetitive business workflows, API integrations and reporting with MV.tech's remote consultants. Reliable jobs, checks and clear ownership.
intro: Connect the steps between your business systems. MV.tech builds API integrations, scheduled workflows and operational automation that reduce repeated manual work and make failures visible.
fit: People repeatedly move the same records between business tools and spreadsheets.
Scheduled reports rely on manual downloads, cleanup and distribution.
An integration works on the happy path but produces duplicate actions after a retry.
A script runs in the background without clear ownership, status checks or recovery steps.
deliverablesHeading: Automation that fits your operating process

deliverables.title: API and webhook integrations
deliverables.text: Connect approved business systems using their supported interfaces. Handle pagination, rate limits, authentication and changes in source records.

deliverables.title: Scheduled business workflows
deliverables.text: Automate recurring data pulls, report preparation, exports and status checks. Define the schedule, inputs and expected output for each step.

deliverables.title: Validation and exception handling
deliverables.text: Add checks before data is written or a downstream action is triggered. Design retries, duplicate prevention and review paths around the impact of a failed step.

deliverables.title: Monitoring and ownership
deliverables.text: Provide logs, useful alerts and operating documentation. Make it clear who maintains a workflow and how to recover or rerun it when a dependency fails.

scopeHeading: A useful first project: one repeated manual handoff
scope: Pick a recurring handoff with a clear input and output, such as preparing a weekly report from several systems. Document what people check today, including exceptions. The project can then automate the repeatable steps while preserving review where judgment is required. Assess the result using completion time, exception frequency and the effort needed to recover a failed run.

approach.title: Observe the current workflow
approach.text: Map triggers, source tools, manual checks, exceptions and who receives the result.

approach.title: Connect and validate
approach.text: Implement the integrations and test retries, missing data and downstream failures as well as a successful run.

approach.title: Schedule and hand over
approach.text: Agree operating hours, alert recipients, access ownership and a recovery procedure.

questions.question: Can you automate a workflow across several tools?
questions.answer: Yes, when the tools provide suitable authorized access. We review available APIs, webhooks, exports and authentication before estimating the integration. Source limits and downstream permissions shape what can be automated reliably.

questions.question: Does every automation need AI?
questions.answer: No. A scheduled job or API integration may be enough for a predictable process. AI is useful when a step requires language or document interpretation, and that step still needs suitable evaluation and review.

questions.question: How do you avoid duplicate records or repeated actions?
questions.answer: The workflow can include stable record identifiers, state tracking, reconciliation and checks before writing. The exact design depends on whether the connected systems support safe retries and how costly a repeated action would be.

questions.question: Can you maintain automations built by another developer?
questions.answer: Yes. An initial review can establish the code, schedules, dependencies, access requirements and failure history. We can then scope a repair, documentation or ongoing support engagement.

name: Custom Software Development
title: Custom Software & Web App Development | MV.tech
description: Hire senior remote developers for business apps, client portals, dashboards and API integrations. MV.tech works alongside your team across timezones.
intro: Build software around the way your business works. MV.tech develops web applications, client portals, dashboards and internal tools, with the interface, data and integrations considered together.
fitHeading: When a custom application makes sense
fit: Your team runs an important process through spreadsheets, email and repeated manual follow-up.
Customers need a portal for records, requests or service updates.
An existing application needs a better interface, a new integration or more reliable reporting.
You need senior development capacity to deliver a defined workstream with your product team.

deliverables.title: Business web applications
deliverables.text: Build responsive interfaces around actual user tasks, data views and permissions. Include loading, empty and error states in the workflow.

deliverables.title: Client portals and internal tools
deliverables.text: Implement role-based access, forms, operational dashboards and approval flows. Agree which actions each user can take and enforce those rules in the application.

deliverables.title: APIs and data backends
deliverables.text: Connect the product to databases, business systems and reporting workflows. Define validation, failure handling and how records stay consistent.

deliverables.title: Release and maintainability
deliverables.text: Scope testing, deployment, monitoring and documentation alongside development. Make future fixes and enhancements part of the handover conversation.

scopeHeading: A useful first project: one complete user journey
scope: Choose a real workflow, such as submitting a request, reviewing it and seeing its status. Agree the roles, data, acceptance criteria and necessary integrations. Delivering that journey end to end gives stakeholders something concrete to evaluate and reveals the operational details that a collection of disconnected screens can miss.

approach.title: Agree the workflow
approach.text: Define users, actions, permissions, existing systems and what a successful release needs to do.

approach.title: Build in reviewable increments
approach.text: Connect interface and backend behavior, review with stakeholders and test important edge cases.

approach.title: Release and support
approach.text: Validate deployment, document ownership and agree how feedback and maintenance will be handled.

questions.question: Can you work in our existing codebase?
questions.answer: Yes. We review the current stack, conventions, deployment process and priorities before proposing changes. A bounded feature or integration is often a useful first engagement.

questions.question: Do you build both the interface and the backend?
questions.answer: Yes. Our services cover responsive interfaces, API-backed workflows, data ingestion, warehouse models and deployment handover. The project scope defines which parts your team and ours will own.

questions.question: How do you estimate a custom software project?
questions.answer: The estimate depends on user journeys, roles, integrations, data migration, testing and release requirements. We scope an initial milestone and clarify assumptions before treating a feature list as a delivery commitment.

questions.question: Can remote developers overlap our working hours?
questions.answer: Yes. MV.tech is remote-first and can plan overlap with teams in any timezone. We agree recurring collaboration windows for reviews and releases, supported by written updates between meetings.

questions.answer: With staff augmentation, consultants add capacity within your team and work under the agreed direction of your technical or delivery leads. A project engagement gives MV.tech ownership of a defined scope and its deliverables. Responsibilities should be explicit in either model.

questions.question: Can we hire a dedicated remote team rather than one consultant?

questions.question: Can consultants overlap our timezone?
questions.answer: Yes. We can plan overlap with clients in any timezone. Share the working hours you need and any release requirements so collaboration windows can be agreed. This does not imply round-the-clock support.

questions.question: Do you also recruit permanent employees?
questions.answer: Yes. MV.tech also offers technology recruitment for permanent roles within a client's organization. Recruitment and consultant staffing are separate engagements with their own scope and commercial terms.

closingHeading: Tell us about the role you are hiring for.

fitHeading: A hiring partner who understands the technical work
fit: You need to hire a permanent engineer or specialist into your own organization.
A role spans AI, data, software or cloud skills that need a clear technical brief.
Your hiring team needs support finding and assessing candidates for an agreed position.
You want candidate conversations grounded in responsibilities, technical depth and the way your team works.

deliverables.title: Candidate sourcing and shortlisting

approachHeading: From hiring brief to a considered selection.

approach.title: Align on the role

approach.title: Source and assess fit
approach.text: Identify candidates against the agreed brief, discuss relevant experience and coordinate your team's assessment.

approach.title: Support the hiring decision

questions.question: How does permanent recruitment differ from staff augmentation?
questions.answer: Permanent recruitment helps you hire an employee into your own organization. Staff augmentation supplies consultants to work within your team for an agreed engagement. MV.tech offers both, and we clarify which arrangement you need before discussing candidates or consultants.

questions.question: Which technology roles can we discuss?
questions.answer: Our focus includes AI and automation, data engineering, software development, cloud platforms, BI and analytics. Share the specific role and experience level so we can assess whether the search fits our technical focus.

questions.question: Can you help with remote technology hiring?
questions.answer: Yes. Share the permitted hiring locations, remote policy, required working hours and employment arrangement. These constraints shape candidate suitability and should be clear before the search begins.

questions.question: What are your recruitment fees and hiring timelines?
questions.answer: Fees, search scope, expected timing and any follow-up terms are agreed for the specific role. Complexity, seniority, compensation, location and interview availability affect the search. We do not promise a hire or a fixed start date before assessing the requirement.
